public_context: Nadia, 42, organizes a monthly extended-family dinner that her 74-year-old father, Tomas, attended reliably for years. Since spring he has declined every invitation with vague excuses, and other relatives are starting to feel hurt and confused. Nadia remains on warm terms with her father and sees him regularly outside these dinners.
initial_request: Can you help me figure out how to persuade my father to start coming to our family dinners again?

ground_truth.expected_problem_formulation: The issue is how the family can restore Tomas's comfortable participation given that his avoidance stems from difficulty following group conversation in noisy settings and embarrassment about being seen as declining, not from a genuine rift with his son-in-law Marc.
ground_truth.problem_formulation_rationale: Early information about the March dinner, where Tomas snapped at Marc and then stopped attending, plausibly supports framing this as a family conflict needing reconciliation. The neighbor's confidential account reverses that reading by showing Tomas misheard Marc and avoids gatherings because he cannot follow noisy group conversation and fears appearing diminished, so treating persuasion or reconciliation as the problem would miss the real barrier.
ground_truth.expected_resolution: Adjust the gatherings toward a quieter, smaller format Tomas can manage, have Nadia privately and non-judgmentally acknowledge his difficulty and encourage a hearing check on his own terms, and treat the Marc incident as a misunderstanding to be gently cleared up rather than staging a formal reconciliation or pressuring him to return.
ground_truth.resolution_rationale: The dinners take place at a loud restaurant with ten or more people, exactly the setting Tomas admits he cannot follow, and he has already refused a hearing screening out of pride, so pressure or a staged apology with Marc would deepen his shame without removing the barrier. Changing the environment and offering discreet support addresses the actual cause while preserving his dignity and the family relationships.

hidden_facts.content: Tomas stopped attending right after the March dinner, where he abruptly snapped at his son-in-law Marc during the meal and left early.
